questions.question: The brachial plexus is formed by the ventral rami of:
questions.explanation: Roots C5–T1 → trunks (upper, middle, lower) → divisions → cords (lateral, medial, posterior) → branches.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The axillary nerve supplies the:
questions.explanation: Arises from the posterior cord (C5–C6); sensory to the regimental badge area.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The musculocutaneous nerve supplies:
questions.explanation: It pierces coracobrachialis; ends as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The radial nerve supplies all of the following muscles EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Radial nerve: all extensors of the arm and forearm, brachioradialis and supinator.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The median nerve supplies which intrinsic hand muscles?

options.D: Thenar muscles (except adductor pollicis) and first two lumbricals (LOAF)

questions.explanation: LOAF: Lateral two Lumbricals, Opponens pollicis, Abductor pollicis brevis, Flexor pollicis brevis (superficial head).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The ulnar nerve supplies:

options.A: Flexor carpi ulnaris, medial half of flexor digitorum profundus, hypothenar muscles, interossei and adductor pollicis

questions.explanation: It passes behind the medial epicondyle (the ‘funny bone’).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The long thoracic nerve (C5–C7) supplies the:
questions.explanation: Injury results in winging of the scapula.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which muscle is NOT part of the rotator cuff?
questions.explanation: SITS: Supraspinatus, Infraspinatus, Teres minor, Subscapularis.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The supraspinatus is supplied by the:
questions.explanation: Suprascapular nerve (C5–C6) also supplies infraspinatus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: How many carpal bones are there and how are they arranged?

options.D: Eight, in two rows of four

questions.explanation: Proximal row: scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform. Distal: trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which carpal bone does NOT articulate with the radius or the ulna's articular disc in the proximal row?
questions.explanation: The pisiform is a sesamoid bone in the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The ulnar nerve and artery pass through Guyon's canal adjacent to the:

options.D: Hook of the hamate and pisiform

questions.explanation: Guyon's canal is bounded medially by the pisiform and laterally by the hook of hamate.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The floor of the anatomical snuffbox is formed by the:
questions.explanation: Boundaries: EPL (medial), EPB and APL (lateral); radial artery crosses the floor.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The structure lying MEDIAL to the biceps tendon in the cubital fossa is the:
questions.explanation: From lateral to medial: radial nerve (deep), biceps tendon, brachial artery, median nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which structure passes OUTSIDE (superficial to) the flexor retinaculum?
questions.explanation: Also the ulnar nerve and artery.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The most important factor maintaining stability of the shoulder joint is the:
questions.explanation: The shallow glenoid and loose capsule favour mobility at the expense of stability.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The only bony articulation between the upper limb and the axial skeleton is the:
questions.explanation: It has a fibrocartilaginous disc dividing it into two cavities.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The dermatome of the middle finger is:
questions.explanation: C6 thumb, C7 middle, C8 little finger.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The femoral nerve (L2–L4) supplies:
questions.explanation: It passes under the inguinal ligament lateral to the femoral artery.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The sciatic nerve divides into the tibial and common peroneal nerves at about the:

options.C: Upper angle of the popliteal fossa

questions.explanation: It leaves the pelvis via the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The obturator nerve supplies:
questions.explanation: Passes through the obturator canal; also gives cutaneous supply to the medial thigh.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The superior gluteal nerve supplies the:

options.D: Gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae

questions.explanation: Injury leads to a Trendelenburg gait.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Gluteus maximus is supplied by the:
questions.explanation: It is the chief extensor of the hip and powerful in climbing stairs.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The common peroneal nerve winds around the:
questions.explanation: It divides into superficial and deep peroneal nerves; injury causes foot drop.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which muscle is NOT supplied by the tibial nerve?
questions.explanation: Tibialis anterior is a dorsiflexor supplied by the deep peroneal nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which head of quadriceps femoris crosses both hip and knee?
questions.explanation: It flexes the hip and extends the knee.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The hamstring muscles arise from the:
questions.explanation: Except the short head of biceps femoris, which arises from the linea aspera.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which muscles form the pes anserinus at the medial tibia?
questions.explanation: Mnemonic: Say Grace before Tea.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The anterior cruciate ligament prevents:

options.A: Anterior displacement of the tibia on the femur

questions.explanation: ACL arises from the posteromedial aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and inserts into the anterior intercondylar area.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The medial meniscus is:

options.B: C-shaped and attached to the medial collateral ligament

questions.explanation: The lateral meniscus is nearly circular, more mobile and separated from the LCL by the popliteus tendon.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The action of the popliteus at the start of knee flexion is to:

options.C: Unlock the knee by medial rotation of the tibia on the femur

questions.explanation: ‘The key that unlocks the knee.’
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The main blood supply to the head of the femur in adults is through the:

options.C: Retinacular branches of the medial circumflex femoral artery
options.D: Artery of the ligamentum teres only

questions.explanation: Intracapsular fractures disrupt this supply — risk of avascular necrosis.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The ankle joint is most stable in:

options.D: Dorsiflexion (close-packed), because the wider anterior talus fits tightly in the mortise

questions.explanation: In plantar flexion the narrower posterior part of the talus lies in the mortise, allowing slight side-to-side movement and sprains.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The most commonly sprained ligament of the ankle is the:
questions.explanation: Due to inversion injury.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The keystone of the medial longitudinal arch of the foot is the:
questions.explanation: The talus receives body weight and distributes it forward and backward.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The tendo calcaneus (Achilles) is formed by the tendons of:

options.A: Tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus

questions.explanation: It inserts on the posterior surface of the calcaneus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: From lateral to medial, the contents of the femoral triangle are:
questions.explanation: Mnemonic NAVEL.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The adductor (Hunter's) canal transmits the:

options.D: Femoral artery and vein, saphenous nerve and the nerve to vastus medialis

questions.explanation: The canal ends at the adductor hiatus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The great saphenous vein begins at the:

options.B: Medial end of the dorsal venous arch of the foot and passes anterior to the medial malleolus

questions.explanation: It drains into the femoral vein at the saphenous opening; the commonest site for venous cut-down.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm at the level of:
questions.explanation: T8: IVC; T10: oesophagus; T12: aorta (with thoracic duct and azygos vein).
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The phrenic nerve originates from:
questions.explanation: Motor to the diaphragm and sensory to central diaphragmatic pleura; referred pain to the shoulder tip.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The right lung has how many lobes and bronchopulmonary segments?
questions.explanation: The left lung has 2 lobes and 8–10 segments with the lingula.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: An inhaled foreign body most commonly lodges in the:
questions.explanation: The right main bronchus is shorter, wider and more vertical.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The artery most commonly involved in anterior wall myocardial infarction is the:
questions.explanation: The ‘widow-maker’ supplies the anterior LV wall and interventricular septum.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The external intercostal muscles are mainly muscles of:
questions.explanation: Fibres run downward and forward; elevate the ribs in the ‘bucket-handle’ and ‘pump-handle’ movement.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The facial nerve (VII) supplies:
questions.explanation: The trigeminal nerve (V3) supplies muscles of mastication.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which muscle opens the mouth (depresses the mandible) against resistance?
questions.explanation: The lateral pterygoid protrudes and depresses the mandible; masseter, temporalis and medial pterygoid close the jaw.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The temporomandibular joint most commonly dislocates:

options.C: Anteriorly, as the condyle moves in front of the articular eminence

questions.explanation: Yawning, seizures or dental procedures can precipitate it.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The spinal accessory nerve (XI) supplies:
questions.explanation: Damage causes shoulder drooping and weakness of shrugging.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The nerve that supplies the lateral rectus muscle of the eye is the:
questions.explanation: LR6 SO4 and the rest are supplied by the oculomotor nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: In an adult the spinal cord ends (conus medullaris) at the level of:
questions.explanation: Lumbar puncture is done at L3–L4 or L4–L5.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Most corticospinal fibres cross the midline at the:

options.C: Pyramidal decussation in the lower medulla

questions.explanation: The lateral corticospinal tract controls limb muscles; the anterior tract is small.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Degeneration of dopaminergic neurones of the substantia nigra causes:
questions.explanation: Huntington's is caused by degeneration of the caudate nucleus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Lesions of one cerebellar hemisphere produce symptoms:
questions.explanation: Intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, nystagmus and hypotonia.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Broca's area of the dominant hemisphere lies in the:
questions.explanation: Wernicke's area is in the posterior superior temporal gyrus.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The primary motor cortex (area 4) lies in the:
questions.explanation: The leg area is on the medial surface, supplied by the ACA.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The circle of Willis is formed by branches of the:
questions.explanation: It allows collateral circulation; the berry aneurysm commonly occurs at the junction of the anterior communicating artery.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The clavicle is unique because it:

options.A: Is a long bone with a medullary canal
options.B: Ossifies in membrane and also has a cartilaginous growth centre at its ends
options.C: Is the last bone to ossify

questions.explanation: It begins ossifying around the 5th–6th week of intrauterine life, the first bone to ossify.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a typical synovial joint?

options.A: A synovial membrane secreting synovial fluid
options.C: Articular hyaline cartilage covering the bone ends
options.D: A fibrous tissue bridge between the bones with no joint cavity

questions.explanation: A synovial joint has a joint cavity with synovial fluid, a capsule and articular cartilage; a fibrous joint has tissue directly uniting the bones with no cavity.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: Smooth muscle is found in:

options.D: The walls of blood vessels and hollow viscera

questions.explanation: Involuntary and non-striated; innervated by the autonomic nervous system.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference

questions.question: The right lymphatic duct drains lymph from:

options.B: The right upper quadrant of the body (right arm, right side of head and thorax)

questions.explanation: The thoracic duct drains the rest.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
